summary: Section S — full event/SLA automation-trigger acceptance suite implemented as /app/backend/tests/test_section_s.py (10 tests). All 10 Section S tests PASS. Regression: 128/129 pre-existing tests pass; the single failure (test_laravel_crm.py::TestLeadCapture::test_verify_task_created) is a pre-existing pagination bug in the old suite — its verify task IS created correctly (confirmed by Section S), but the old test hits GET /tasks with default per_page=25 and the session-scoped seed_lead's task now falls off page 1 as other tests create more tasks. Not a Section S regression.

minor.issue: No server-side filter by lead_id — clients must paginate and filter locally. Consider adding ?lead_id= query param for efficiency.

Pre-existing test relies on default pagination (25) without lead_id filter; fails once >25 tasks exist. Test should use ?lead_id={id} filter (as Section S does). Verify task functionality itself works correctly.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Fix pre-existing test_laravel_crm.py::test_verify_task_created to filter by lead_id (one-line fix — add ?lead_id={seed_lead['id']} to the GET /tasks call). This is unrelated to Section S.
OPTIONAL: Add lead_id query filter to AutomationController::logs for cleaner client integration.
critical_code_review_comments: AutomationService::conditionsMet correctly falls back to context then lead attribute — 'to' condition is passed via LeadService context ['from','to','status'], so status.changed rules bind correctly.
RunReminders assigns to sales_manager role (fallback admin) — deterministic given seeded Priya user.
AutomationLog writes ALL action attempts (success/failed) via try/catch — good for observability. No failed rows observed across all lifecycle events during suite run.
Task creation via automation uses lead.owner_id as assignee (sales exec via round-robin), enabling SLA escalation flow to reassign to manager on breach.
Minor: AutomationController::logs has no lead/rule/event filters — will not scale beyond a few hundred rows.
Minor: RunReminders is a single 145-line handle() method covering 5 concerns (verify, follow_up, site-visit, docs, payments). Consider splitting into per-concern jobs.
test_credentials: admin@crm.local/Admin@12345, priya@crm.local/Demo@12345 (sales_manager id resolved dynamically via GET /api/v1/users)
seed_data_creation: Fresh reseed via `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed --force` executed before suite. Each test creates its own TEST_S_<uuid> lead — isolated per case.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Section S suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_section_s.py. Uses direct Laravel artisan calls (tinker for DB backdating, crm:reminders for escalation) — must run from environment with php + laravel-crm accessible. Sales manager id resolved at runtime via API (not hardcoded to 2). AutomationLog listing has no lead_id filter; suite paginates 200 rows and filters client-side — if per_page becomes limiting, add server-side filter. All 7 seeded automation rules verified end-to-end; no rule fires 'failed' status.
rca of the issue: N/A — Section S acceptance passes fully. Pre-existing regression failure RCA: test_verify_task_created uses unpaginated `GET /tasks` (default per_page=25). With Section S adding ~14 leads → ~28+ tasks, the seed_lead task overflows page 1. Fix: append `?lead_id={id}` to the request (or increase per_page). Not caused by Section S implementation.
